words.enDefinition: A molecule that occurs in living systems and participates in their structure or function.

examples.en: The first diagram shows glucose as a biomolecule used in the energy metabolism of human cells.
examples.zh: 第一幅图把葡萄糖列为参与人体细胞能量代谢的「生物分子」。

examples.en: The class compared one small biomolecule with a much larger protein in the chapter's introductory illustration.
examples.zh: 看本章的导读图时，我们将一种小「生物分子」与一种大得多的蛋白质作比较。

words.enDefinition: A large molecule in a living system, such as a protein or polysaccharide.

examples.en: The tutor used glycogen as an example of a macromolecule with many linked glucose units.
examples.zh: 辅导老师以糖原为例，说明这种「生物大分子」含有许多相连的葡萄糖单元。

examples.en: We traced the outline of the folded macromolecule in the illustration of an ordinary human cell.
examples.zh: 我们在普通人体细胞的插图上沿着折叠的「生物大分子」描出轮廓。

collocations: a macromolecule in a human cell

words.enDefinition: A small molecular building block represented as one unit of a larger polymer.

examples.en: The diagram uses a single glucose shape to represent one monomer unit of the glycogen chain.
examples.zh: 图中用一个葡萄糖形状表示糖原链的一个「单体单元」。

examples.en: We identified the monomer unit shown repeatedly along the chain in our classroom figure of glycogen.
examples.zh: 在课堂糖原图中，我们认出了沿链反复出现的「单体单元」。

collocations: the identity of a monomer unit

words.enDefinition: A natural macromolecule made of covalently linked units derived from smaller molecules.

examples.en: The textbook depicts glycogen as a biological polymer whose glucose units form a branched structure.
examples.zh: 教材把糖原画成一种「生物聚合物」，其葡萄糖单元形成分支结构。

examples.en: We compared the backbone of a biological polymer with the separate building blocks in the labeled drawing.
examples.zh: 在标注图中，我们将「生物聚合物」的主链与单独的构成单元进行了比较。

collocations: the building blocks of a biological polymer

words.enDefinition: A carbohydrate consisting of a single sugar unit.

examples.en: We identified glucose as a monosaccharide because it had one sugar unit in the structure chart.
examples.zh: 结构图中的葡萄糖只有一个糖单元，因此我们将它归为「单糖」。

examples.en: The tutor pointed to each monosaccharide separately before discussing the linked pair shown in the next panel.
examples.zh: 辅导老师先分别指出各个「单糖」，再讲解下一幅图中相连的两个糖单元。

words.enDefinition: A carbohydrate consisting of two monosaccharides connected by a glycosidic bond.

examples.en: The disaccharide in the illustration contained two sugar rings linked through an oxygen atom in the drawing.
examples.zh: 图中的「二糖」含有两个糖环，两者通过一个氧原子相连。

examples.en: We identified the disaccharide by counting two linked monosaccharide units in the textbook diagram.
examples.zh: 我们数出教材图中有两个相连的单糖单元，据此认出了「二糖」。

collocations: the sugar units of a disaccharide

words.enDefinition: A short carbohydrate chain made of a small number of linked sugar units.

examples.en: The small chain on the outside of the human cell membrane was labeled as an oligosaccharide.
examples.zh: 人体细胞膜外侧的一条短链被标为「寡糖」。

examples.en: We compared the oligosaccharide drawing with a longer branched carbohydrate in the model of cell surface molecules.
examples.zh: 在细胞表面分子示意图中，我们把「寡糖」图与较长的支链糖类进行了比较。

collocations: an oligosaccharide attached to a lipid

words.enDefinition: A carbohydrate polymer made of many linked monosaccharide units.

examples.en: The body stores glucose in glycogen, a branched polysaccharide illustrated in the chapter on human metabolism.
examples.zh: 人体以糖原储存葡萄糖，这种支链「多糖」画在人体代谢一章中。

examples.en: We traced several branches of the polysaccharide before identifying the repeating sugar units in the diagram.
examples.zh: 我们先沿「多糖」看了几条分支，再找出图中反复出现的糖单元。

words.enDefinition: A monosaccharide containing six carbon atoms.

examples.en: The tutor labeled glucose as a hexose after counting all its carbon atoms on the structure diagram.
examples.zh: 辅导老师数完结构图中葡萄糖的全部碳原子后，将其标为「己糖」。

examples.en: We counted the carbon outside the glucose ring when deciding whether the molecule was a hexose.
examples.zh: 判断葡萄糖是不是「己糖」时，我们也数上了糖环以外的碳原子。

collocations: the carbon atoms of a hexose

words.enDefinition: A six-carbon sugar used as an energy source and stored in human cells as glycogen.

examples.en: The metabolism map placed glucose at the entrance to the pathway that breaks down the sugar.
examples.zh: 代谢图把「葡萄糖」标在分解这种糖的途径入口。

examples.en: We followed glucose from the single sugar symbol into the branched storage molecule on our worksheet.
examples.zh: 我们在习题中从一个糖分子符号出发，追踪「葡萄糖」进入带分支的储存分子。

words.enDefinition: A six-carbon sugar distinguished from glucose by the location of the carbonyl group in its open-chain form.

examples.en: The diagram labels fructose beside glucose, showing their carbonyl groups at different positions in open chains.
examples.zh: 图中并列标出了「果糖」和葡萄糖，显示两者在开链形式下的羰基位置不同。

examples.en: We traced the arrow showing how human cells can route fructose into a central metabolic pathway.
examples.zh: 我们顺着箭头看人体细胞如何让「果糖」进入一条中央代谢途径。

words.enDefinition: A six-carbon sugar differing from glucose in the arrangement at one carbon atom.

examples.en: The class compared galactose with glucose by checking the orientation of one group on the sugar ring.
examples.zh: 我们核对糖环上一个基团的朝向，用来比较「半乳糖」和葡萄糖。

examples.en: The chart showed galactose as one of the sugar units in a molecule found on human cells.
examples.zh: 图表把「半乳糖」列为人体细胞表面某分子的糖单元之一。

words.enDefinition: A covalent link joining a sugar through its anomeric carbon to another group.

examples.en: We highlighted the glycosidic bond linking two glucose units in the picture of the storage chain.
examples.zh: 我们在储存糖链图中高亮了连接两个葡萄糖单元的「糖苷键」。

examples.en: The tutor marked a different glycosidic bond where the glycogen chain branched in the classroom diagram.
examples.zh: 辅导老师在课堂图里糖原链分支处标出了另一种「糖苷键」。

words.enDefinition: A branched glucose polymer used to store carbohydrate in human cells.

examples.en: The muscle cell diagram shows glycogen as a reserve of glucose units arranged in branched chains.
examples.zh: 肌细胞图将「糖原」画成由支链上的葡萄糖单元构成的储备。

examples.en: We traced the pathway arrow showing how an ordinary human cell adds glucose units to glycogen.
examples.zh: 我们顺着代谢图箭头，看普通人体细胞如何向「糖原」添加葡萄糖单元。

words.enDefinition: A discrete intracellular particle containing stored glycogen and associated proteins.

examples.en: The enlarged cell picture labels a glycogen granule as a small storage particle in the cytoplasm.
examples.zh: 放大的细胞图将「糖原颗粒」标为细胞质中的小型储存颗粒。

examples.en: We matched the glycogen granule in the tissue illustration with the branch pattern in the molecular diagram.
examples.zh: 我们将组织图中的「糖原颗粒」与分子图里的分支结构对应起来。

collocations: a glycogen granule in a cell
the surface of a glycogen granule

words.enDefinition: A storage lipid consisting of glycerol linked by ester bonds to three fatty acids.

examples.en: The diagram shows triacylglycerol with one glycerol backbone and three attached fatty acid chains in total.
examples.zh: 图中「甘油三酯」包含一个甘油骨架，总共连接三条脂肪酸链。

examples.en: We identified triacylglycerol in the textbook illustration of stored lipid droplets inside a human fat cell.
examples.zh: 我们在人体脂肪细胞内储存脂滴的教材图上找到了「甘油三酯」。

words.enDefinition: An organic acid consisting of a hydrocarbon chain and a terminal carboxyl group.

examples.en: We recognized the fatty acid by finding the carboxyl group at one end of its carbon chain.
examples.zh: 我们在碳链一端找到羧基，据此辨认出「脂肪酸」。

examples.en: The cellular diagram shows one fatty acid tail extending toward the center of the membrane layer.
examples.zh: 细胞图显示一条「脂肪酸」尾部伸向膜层中央。

words.enDefinition: A fatty acid with no carbon-carbon double bonds along its hydrocarbon chain.

examples.en: We identified the saturated fatty acid by checking that the carbon chain contained only single bonds.
examples.zh: 我们确认碳链上只有单键，认出了「饱和脂肪酸」。

examples.en: The saturated fatty acid appeared as a comparatively straight chain in the classroom model of membrane lipids.
examples.zh: 在课堂膜脂模型中，「饱和脂肪酸」对应的链条比较直。

collocations: a saturated fatty acid in a lipid

words.enDefinition: A fatty acid with one carbon-carbon double bond in its hydrocarbon chain.

examples.en: The monounsaturated fatty acid in the diagram had a single bend where the marked double bond appeared.
examples.zh: 图中的「单不饱和脂肪酸」在标出的双键处有一处弯折。

examples.en: We identified a monounsaturated fatty acid by counting one carbon-carbon double bond along the pictured chain.
examples.zh: 我们数出图中链上只有一个碳碳双键，据此认出「单不饱和脂肪酸」。

words.enDefinition: A fatty acid with two or more carbon-carbon double bonds in its hydrocarbon chain.

examples.en: The polyunsaturated fatty acid had several marked double bonds in the enlarged illustration we studied.
examples.zh: 我们观察的放大图中，「多不饱和脂肪酸」标出了多个双键。

examples.en: We followed the bends on the polyunsaturated fatty acid drawing to compare it with the straighter chain.
examples.zh: 我们沿「多不饱和脂肪酸」图中的弯折观察，将它与较直的链作比较。

collocations: a polyunsaturated fatty acid in membrane lipids

words.enDefinition: A double bond with the specified reference groups on the same side, as in many natural fatty acids.

examples.en: The classroom drawing showed a cis double bond bending the fatty acid chain away from its straight path.
examples.zh: 课堂图显示，「顺式双键」让脂肪酸链偏离原本的直线走向。

examples.en: We recognized the cis double bond where the two continuing chain segments lay on the same side.
examples.zh: 图中双键两侧继续延伸的链段位于同侧，我们由此认出「顺式双键」。

collocations: a cis double bond in a fatty acid
a bend at a cis double bond

words.enDefinition: The three-carbon glycerol framework to which other groups are attached in a lipid.

examples.en: We traced the glycerol backbone between the fatty acid tails and the polar head in the drawing.
examples.zh: 我们在图中沿着脂肪酸尾与极性头部之间的「甘油骨架」观察。

examples.en: The three attachment positions on the glycerol backbone were labeled in the storage lipid example.
examples.zh: 储存脂示意图标出了「甘油骨架」上的三个连接位置。

collocations: a glycerol backbone in a phospholipid
groups attached to a glycerol backbone

words.enDefinition: A covalent bond characteristic of an ester, such as a fatty acid attachment to glycerol.

examples.en: We marked the ester linkage joining one of the fatty acids to glycerol in the diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在图上标出了把其中一条脂肪酸连接到甘油的「酯键」。

examples.en: The tutor pointed to each ester linkage when explaining the three attachments in the storage lipid illustration.
examples.zh: 辅导老师解释储存脂图中的三处连接时，逐个指出了各个「酯键」。

collocations: an ester linkage in a storage lipid

words.enDefinition: A lipid that forms part of a biological membrane.

examples.en: We identified one membrane lipid with a polar head projecting toward the water outside the cell.
examples.zh: 我们找到一种「膜脂」，其极性头部朝向细胞外的水相。

examples.en: The tutor grouped each membrane lipid by the shape of its polar region in the diagram.
examples.zh: 辅导老师根据极性部分的形状，为图中的各种「膜脂」分组。

words.enDefinition: A lipid containing a phosphate-bearing polar group and a hydrophobic region.

examples.en: The diagram shows each phospholipid with a polar head facing water and tails pointing toward the center.
examples.zh: 图中每个「磷脂」的极性头朝向水相，脂肪链尾朝向中央。

examples.en: We traced the phosphate group on the phospholipid in the close-up drawing of a human cell membrane.
examples.zh: 我们在人体细胞膜放大图上找出「磷脂」中的磷酸基团。

collocations: the head group of a phospholipid

words.enDefinition: Two opposing layers of phospholipids whose tails face inward and heads face the surrounding water.

examples.en: The classroom model shows the phospholipid bilayer separating the surrounding fluid from the inside of a cell.
examples.zh: 课堂模型展示了「磷脂双层」如何将周围液体与细胞内部隔开。

examples.en: We placed the tail arrows in the middle of the phospholipid bilayer in our sketch of the membrane.
examples.zh: 我们在膜的草图中把尾部箭头画在「磷脂双层」的中央。

collocations: the inner side of a phospholipid bilayer

words.enDefinition: A polar part of a membrane lipid that interacts with the surrounding water.

examples.en: The polar head group faced the watery cytoplasm in the diagram of the inner membrane layer.
examples.zh: 膜内层的图中，「极性头基」朝向富含水分的细胞质。

examples.en: We compared the polar head group structures shown on two phospholipids in the classroom illustration.
examples.zh: 我们比较了课堂插图中两种磷脂所带的「极性头基」结构。

collocations: the size of a polar head group

words.enDefinition: A nonpolar region of an amphipathic molecule that tends to avoid contact with water.

examples.en: The hydrophobic tail pointed inward where it contacted other nonpolar tails in the simplified membrane diagram.
examples.zh: 在简化膜图中，「疏水尾部」朝内，与其他非极性的尾部接触。

examples.en: We labeled the hydrophobic tail where it extended toward the center of the bilayer in the diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在图中伸向双层中央的位置标出了「疏水尾部」。

collocations: a hydrophobic tail of a lipid
the position of a hydrophobic tail

words.enDefinition: A molecule containing both water-interacting and water-avoiding regions.

examples.en: We classified the phospholipid as an amphipathic molecule because its head and tails interact differently with water.
examples.zh: 磷脂头部和尾部与水的相互作用不同，因此我们把它归为「两亲性分子」。

examples.en: The tutor colored both regions of the amphipathic molecule to explain its orientation in the membrane sketch.
examples.zh: 辅导老师为「两亲性分子」的两个区域着色，解释它在膜草图中的朝向。

collocations: an amphipathic molecule in a membrane
the regions of an amphipathic molecule

words.enDefinition: The ease with which lipids and other components can move within a membrane.

examples.en: The animation illustrated membrane fluidity by showing phospholipids moving sideways within the same layer of a membrane.
examples.zh: 动画让磷脂在同一膜层内横向移动，以说明「膜流动性」。

examples.en: We discussed membrane fluidity when comparing diagrams of a loosely packed layer and a more ordered layer.
examples.zh: 我们比较排列较松散的膜层与较有序的膜层图示时，讨论了「膜流动性」。

collocations: the effect of lipid composition on membrane fluidity

words.enDefinition: Cholesterol incorporated among other lipids in a cell membrane, where it influences their packing and mobility.

examples.en: The drawing positions membrane cholesterol among the lipid tails in a section of the human cell membrane.
examples.zh: 人体细胞膜的切面图把「膜胆固醇」画在脂质尾部之间。

examples.en: We identified the small polar group of membrane cholesterol near the head groups on the membrane diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在膜图的头基附近，找到了「膜胆固醇」的小极性基团。

collocations: the effect of membrane cholesterol on fluidity

words.enDefinition: A lipid bearing an attached carbohydrate group.

examples.en: The text shows the sugar portion of a glycolipid projecting outward from the human cell membrane.
examples.zh: 教材显示，「糖脂」的糖部分从人体细胞膜向外伸出。

examples.en: We distinguished the glycolipid in the figure by following its attached sugar chain toward the cell exterior.
examples.zh: 我们在图中沿向细胞外伸展的连接糖链，认出了「糖脂」。

collocations: the sugar group of a glycolipid
a glycolipid on the cell surface

words.enDefinition: A lipid built around a sphingoid base rather than a glycerol backbone.

examples.en: Our worksheet labeled the sphingolipid by pointing to its distinct backbone on the membrane comparison chart.
examples.zh: 习题在膜成分比较图中指向特有骨架，为「鞘脂」作出标注。

examples.en: We compared the head groups of one sphingolipid and one glycerol-based lipid in the textbook illustration.
examples.zh: 我们比较了教材图中一种「鞘脂」和一种以甘油为骨架的脂质的头基。

words.enDefinition: The differing composition or orientation of components on the two sides of a biological membrane.

examples.en: The membrane asymmetry diagram showed sugar chains exposed mainly on the outward face of the cell.
examples.zh: 「膜不对称性」图显示，糖链主要暴露在细胞的外表面。

examples.en: We explained membrane asymmetry by comparing the lipid types drawn on the inner and outer layers.
examples.zh: 我们比较内外两层中画出的脂质类型，解释「膜不对称性」。

words.enDefinition: An organic compound with amino and carboxyl groups, serving as a protein building block in this context.

examples.en: The textbook shows an amino acid beside a short chain made from several linked units.
examples.zh: 教材把一个「氨基酸」与由若干单元相连的短链画在一起。

examples.en: We identified each amino acid on the chart by comparing the groups attached to its central carbon.
examples.zh: 我们比较各分子中心碳原子所连的基团，辨认表上的各种「氨基酸」。

collocations: the structure of an amino acid
an amino acid in a protein chain

words.enDefinition: The carbon next to the carboxyl group that bears the amino group in a protein-forming amino acid.

examples.en: The molecular picture places the amino group and the side chain around the same alpha carbon.
examples.zh: 分子图中，氨基和侧链都连接在同一个「α碳原子」上。

examples.en: We counted the groups attached to the alpha carbon of glycine in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂模型中数出甘氨酸「α碳原子」连接的基团。

collocations: a side chain on the alpha carbon
the groups around an alpha carbon

words.enDefinition: A nitrogen-containing group of the form NH2, which may carry a proton in aqueous environments.

examples.en: The illustration labels the amino group at one side of the central carbon in the free molecule.
examples.zh: 插图在游离分子中心碳原子的一侧标出了「氨基」。

examples.en: We circled the amino group on the free amino acid before looking at the peptide diagram.
examples.zh: 我们先圈出游离氨基酸上的「氨基」，再看肽的示意图。

collocations: an amino group on an amino acid

words.enDefinition: The acidic group containing a carbonyl and a hydroxyl on the same carbon, often present as carboxylate in cells.

examples.en: We recognized the carboxyl group by the two oxygen atoms attached to the same carbon in the illustration.
examples.zh: 我们看到插图中同一碳原子连着两个氧原子，据此找出「羧基」。

examples.en: The chart marks the carboxyl group at one end of the isolated amino acid drawing.
examples.zh: 图表在单独画出的氨基酸一端标出了「羧基」。

collocations: the charge associated with a carboxyl group

words.enDefinition: The variable group attached to an amino acid's alpha carbon that distinguishes it from other amino acids.

examples.en: The chart distinguishes each amino acid side chain while drawing the shared backbone in the same way.
examples.zh: 图表以相同方式绘出共同的骨架，分别标示各个「氨基酸侧链」。

examples.en: We highlighted one amino acid side chain to explain why two residues behave differently near water.
examples.zh: 我们高亮一条「氨基酸侧链」，解释两个残基靠近水时为何表现不同。

collocations: identify an amino acid side chain
a charged amino acid side chain
interactions of an amino acid side chain

words.enDefinition: A molecule with both positively and negatively charged groups and a net charge of zero.

examples.en: The glycine drawing shows a zwitterion with opposite charges on two groups and no overall charge.
examples.zh: 甘氨酸图所示的「两性离子」在两个基团上带相反电荷，净电荷为零。

examples.en: We recognized the zwitterion by checking both marked charges in the classroom drawing of the molecule.
examples.zh: 我们核对课堂分子图标出的两处电荷，认出了「两性离子」。

words.enDefinition: An amino acid that humans cannot synthesize in sufficient amounts and obtain from their diet.

examples.en: The textbook lists leucine as an essential amino acid in its table of human amino acids.
examples.zh: 教材的人体氨基酸表把亮氨酸列为「必需氨基酸」。

examples.en: We discussed why an essential amino acid appears on a chart showing sources of protein building blocks.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么说明蛋白质构成单元来源的图表会列出「必需氨基酸」。

collocations: an essential amino acid in human nutrition
the requirement for an essential amino acid

words.enDefinition: An amino acid the body can normally synthesize in sufficient amounts.

examples.en: The chart uses alanine as a nonessential amino acid that ordinary human cells can make.
examples.zh: 图表以丙氨酸为「非必需氨基酸」示例，普通人体细胞能够生成它。

examples.en: Our tutor explained that a nonessential amino acid still has important roles in human proteins.
examples.zh: 辅导老师解释，「非必需氨基酸」在人体蛋白质中仍发挥重要作用。

collocations: formation of a nonessential amino acid

words.enDefinition: An amino acid with a branched aliphatic side chain, such as leucine, isoleucine, or valine.

examples.en: We identified leucine as a branched-chain amino acid by tracing the carbon branch in its structure.
examples.zh: 我们沿结构图观察亮氨酸的碳链分支，将它归为「支链氨基酸」。

examples.en: The chart placed valine in the branched-chain amino acid group beside two other similar molecules.
examples.zh: 图表将缬氨酸放入「支链氨基酸」一组，旁边列出另外两个相似分子。

collocations: an example of a branched-chain amino acid

words.enDefinition: An amino acid side chain containing groups that can interact strongly with water.

examples.en: The polar side chain on the protein diagram faced the water surrounding the folded molecule.
examples.zh: 蛋白质图中的「极性侧链」朝向折叠分子周围的水相。

examples.en: We marked a polar side chain beside the diagram's example of a hydrogen bond with water.
examples.zh: 我们在图中与水形成氢键的示例旁标出一条「极性侧链」。

collocations: a polar side chain on a protein surface

words.enDefinition: An amino acid side chain lacking strongly polar groups and interacting weakly with water.

examples.en: The example shows a nonpolar side chain tucked inside the folded protein away from surrounding water.
examples.zh: 示例把一条「非极性侧链」画在折叠蛋白质内部，远离周围的水。

examples.en: We traced the carbon groups in the nonpolar side chain shown on the amino acid chart.
examples.zh: 我们沿氨基酸图表找出了「非极性侧链」上的各个碳基团。

collocations: packing of a nonpolar side chain

words.enDefinition: An amino acid side chain with a group that can donate a proton and often carries negative charge.

examples.en: The diagram labels the negatively charged group of an acidic side chain in the folded protein.
examples.zh: 图中标出了折叠蛋白质中一条「酸性侧链」带负电的基团。

examples.en: We located the additional carboxyl group on the acidic side chain in the classroom structure chart.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂结构图中，找到了「酸性侧链」上额外的羧基。

collocations: a negatively charged acidic side chain
an acidic side chain in a protein

words.enDefinition: An amino acid side chain with a group that can accept a proton.

examples.en: The textbook showed one basic side chain carrying a positive charge at the stated cellular pH.
examples.zh: 教材显示，在所给的细胞 pH 条件下，一条「碱性侧链」带正电。

examples.en: We compared a basic side chain with the uncharged polar group drawn beside it in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们把「碱性侧链」与旁边画出的不带电极性基团相比较。

collocations: a positively charged basic side chain
a basic side chain in a protein

words.enDefinition: The amide linkage between the carboxyl carbon of one amino acid residue and the nitrogen of another.

examples.en: We marked the peptide bond between the first two residues in the short chain diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在短链图中标出了前两个残基之间的「肽键」。

examples.en: The tutor showed where the peptide bond sat along the shared backbone of the pictured segments.
examples.zh: 辅导老师指出，「肽键」在图示各片段共同的骨架上处于哪里。

collocations: a peptide bond in the backbone

words.enDefinition: The part of an amino acid that forms a unit of a peptide or protein chain.

examples.en: We labeled one amino acid residue in the classroom drawing of a longer human protein chain.
examples.zh: 我们在较长的人体蛋白质链课堂图中标出一个「氨基酸残基」。

examples.en: The chart identifies each amino acid residue by its side chain and position in the sequence.
examples.zh: 图表按侧链和序列位置辨认各个「氨基酸残基」。

collocations: an amino acid residue in a chain
the side chain of an amino acid residue

words.enDefinition: A chain of amino acid residues linked by peptide bonds.

examples.en: The illustration shows a polypeptide as a continuous chain with side groups drawn along its backbone.
examples.zh: 插图把「多肽」画成一条连续的链，侧基沿骨架分布。

examples.en: We followed the polypeptide through the drawing to see where it folded back toward its center.
examples.zh: 我们沿图中的「多肽」观察，看它在哪里折回自身中央。

words.enDefinition: The end of a polypeptide corresponding to the first residue's backbone amino group.

examples.en: The textbook starts the sequence at the amino terminus and reads toward the other end.
examples.zh: 教材从「氨基端」开始写序列，依次读到另一端。

examples.en: We marked the amino terminus on the protein diagram before tracing the chain into the folded region.
examples.zh: 我们在蛋白质图上先标出「氨基端」，再沿链观察折叠区。

collocations: the amino terminus of a polypeptide

words.enDefinition: The end of a polypeptide corresponding to the final residue's backbone carboxyl group.

examples.en: The carboxyl terminus appears at the final residue of the chain in our classroom drawing.
examples.zh: 课堂图中，「羧基端」位于链的最后一个残基。

examples.en: We traced the protein backbone to the carboxyl terminus on the right side of the figure.
examples.zh: 我们沿蛋白质骨架追踪到图中右侧的「羧基端」。

collocations: the carboxyl terminus of a polypeptide

words.enDefinition: The sequence of amino acid residues in a protein's polypeptide chain or chains.

examples.en: The figure represents protein primary structure as a line of residue names in their sequence order.
examples.zh: 图中用按序排列的一行残基名称表示「蛋白质一级结构」。

examples.en: We compared protein primary structure before looking at the folded shapes shown in the next panel.
examples.zh: 我们先比较「蛋白质一级结构」，再看下一幅图中的折叠形状。

collocations: a diagram of protein primary structure

words.enDefinition: Local patterns in a protein backbone, such as helices or sheets stabilized by backbone hydrogen bonds.

examples.en: The spiral and the sheet illustrate two kinds of protein secondary structure in the textbook drawing.
examples.zh: 教材图中的螺旋和片层说明了两种「蛋白质二级结构」。

examples.en: We found protein secondary structure by locating repeated backbone shapes in the classroom model of the chain.
examples.zh: 我们在链的课堂模型中寻找反复出现的骨架形态，以辨认「蛋白质二级结构」。

collocations: common patterns of protein secondary structure
a region of protein secondary structure

words.enDefinition: The overall three-dimensional arrangement of one folded polypeptide chain.

examples.en: The instructor used a folded chain model to show protein tertiary structure from several viewing angles.
examples.zh: 老师用一个折叠链模型，从多个角度展示「蛋白质三级结构」。

examples.en: The protein tertiary structure diagram showed two regions of the same chain lying close together after folding.
examples.zh: 「蛋白质三级结构」图显示，折叠后同一条链上的两个区域靠在一起。

collocations: the stability of protein tertiary structure
a model of protein tertiary structure

words.enDefinition: The arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits in one functional protein assembly.

examples.en: The multicolored figure used a different shade for each chain to illustrate protein quaternary structure.
examples.zh: 多色图给每条链用了不同颜色，以展示「蛋白质四级结构」。

examples.en: We discussed protein quaternary structure when the diagram showed two separate chains forming one assembly.
examples.zh: 图中两条独立的链组成一个复合结构，我们借此讨论了「蛋白质四级结构」。

collocations: a model of protein quaternary structure

words.enDefinition: A common coiled protein backbone structure stabilized by hydrogen bonds within the same chain segment.

examples.en: The alpha helix was drawn as a coil in one region of the simplified protein model.
examples.zh: 在简化的蛋白质模型中，有一个区域画成卷曲状，表示「α螺旋」。

examples.en: We traced the repeating backbone pattern around the alpha helix in the chapter's close-up drawing.
examples.zh: 我们在本章的放大图上沿「α螺旋」辨认重复的骨架排列。

collocations: an alpha helix in a protein
backbone bonds within an alpha helix

words.enDefinition: A protein backbone structure formed by neighboring strands linked by backbone hydrogen bonds.

examples.en: The beta sheet looked like several arrows arranged side by side in the classroom ribbon drawing.
examples.zh: 课堂丝带图上的「β折叠」看起来像几个并排的箭头。

examples.en: We compared the strand directions within the beta sheet shown in the textbook's labeled model.
examples.zh: 我们比较了教材标注模型中「β折叠」内各条链段的方向。

collocations: identify a beta sheet in a protein

words.enDefinition: A covalent link between the sulfur atoms of two cysteine residues.

examples.en: The illustration shows a disulfide bond joining two distant regions of the same folded chain.
examples.zh: 插图显示，一条「二硫键」连接同一折叠链上原本相距很远的两个区域。

examples.en: We marked the two sulfur atoms on either side of the disulfide bond in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们标出了「二硫键」两侧的两个硫原子。

collocations: a protein stabilized by a disulfide bond

words.enDefinition: The process by which a polypeptide acquires its usual three-dimensional shape.

examples.en: The animation illustrates protein folding by bringing distant regions of one polypeptide close to each other.
examples.zh: 动画让同一条多肽上相距很远的区域靠近，以展示「蛋白质折叠」。

examples.en: We discussed protein folding after comparing the straight sequence drawing with the folded molecular shape.
examples.zh: 我们比较了直线排列的序列图和折叠后的分子形状，随后讨论了「蛋白质折叠」。

collocations: protein folding in a human cell

words.enDefinition: The usual three-dimensional arrangement associated with a protein's function under its normal conditions.

examples.en: The model shows the native protein conformation beside an unfolded version of the same chain.
examples.zh: 模型把「蛋白质天然构象」与同一条链的未折叠形式并列画出。

examples.en: We identified the native protein conformation by matching the drawing to the caption about the protein's function.
examples.zh: 我们将结构图与说明蛋白质功能的图注对应起来，辨认出「蛋白质天然构象」。

collocations: the shape of a native protein conformation
compare a native protein conformation with an unfolded form

words.enDefinition: A distinct region of a protein that folds as a unit and may have a particular function.

examples.en: The labeled model showed one protein domain as a compact region within a much longer chain.
examples.zh: 标注模型将一个「蛋白质结构域」画成较长链中紧凑的一部分。

examples.en: We colored each protein domain separately to highlight the two organized regions in the diagram.
examples.zh: 我们给图中各「蛋白质结构域」分别着色，以突出两个成形的区域。

collocations: the structure of a protein domain

words.enDefinition: An individual polypeptide component of a protein complex with multiple chains.

examples.en: The diagram assigned a different color to each protein subunit in the normal human protein assembly.
examples.zh: 图中给正常人体蛋白质复合物的每个「蛋白质亚基」用了不同颜色。

examples.en: We followed one protein subunit from the side view to its matching label in the top view.
examples.zh: 我们从侧视图追踪一个「蛋白质亚基」，在俯视图中找到对应标记。

collocations: a protein subunit in a complex

words.enDefinition: A change in a protein's three-dimensional arrangement without a change in its amino acid sequence.

examples.en: The animation illustrates a protein conformational change as two regions shift closer together during ordinary cellular activity.
examples.zh: 动画中，细胞正常活动时蛋白质的两个区域彼此靠近，展示了「蛋白质构象变化」。

examples.en: We compared the two drawings to identify the protein conformational change within the same folded chain.
examples.zh: 我们对比两幅图，辨认同一折叠链中发生的「蛋白质构象变化」。

collocations: a protein conformational change during binding

words.enDefinition: Loss of a protein's native three-dimensional structure, typically with its primary chain sequence intact.

examples.en: The diagram illustrates protein denaturation by showing a compact folded shape becoming less ordered in the model.
examples.zh: 示意图把紧凑的折叠形状逐渐变得无序的过程画出，以说明「蛋白质变性」。

examples.en: We compared the two textbook panels to see which structural levels changed during protein denaturation.
examples.zh: 我们对比教材中的两幅图，查看「蛋白质变性」时哪些结构层次发生了变化。

collocations: a loss of structure during protein denaturation

words.enDefinition: A protein that assists other proteins in folding or prevents inappropriate interactions between them.

examples.en: The cell diagram shows a molecular chaperone interacting temporarily with another protein as that protein folds.
examples.zh: 细胞图显示，另一种蛋白质折叠时，「分子伴侣」暂时与其相互作用。

examples.en: We identified the molecular chaperone beside the folding chain in the model of a human cell.
examples.zh: 我们在人体细胞模型中的折叠链旁找到了「分子伴侣」。

collocations: a molecular chaperone in the cytoplasm
the role of a molecular chaperone

words.enDefinition: A biological catalyst, usually a protein, that speeds a reaction without being consumed overall.

examples.en: The diagram labels each enzyme above the reaction arrow it helps the human cell carry out.
examples.zh: 图中在各个反应箭头上方标出帮助人体细胞完成该反应的「酶」。

examples.en: The lecturer described an enzyme as a catalyst while tracing the sequence on the metabolism map.
examples.zh: 老师沿代谢图讲解反应顺序时，将「酶」描述为催化剂。

collocations: an enzyme in a human cell

words.enDefinition: A molecule acted upon by an enzyme during a reaction.

examples.en: The figure depicts an enzyme substrate entering the shaded pocket before the illustrated chemical change.
examples.zh: 图中，一种「酶底物」进入有阴影的凹槽，随后发生图示的化学变化。

examples.en: We followed the enzyme substrate from its first appearance to the later product in the diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在图上追踪「酶底物」从最初出现到形成后续产物的过程。

collocations: the shape of an enzyme substrate

words.enDefinition: The part of an enzyme where a substrate binds and catalysis takes place.

examples.en: The drawing marks the enzyme active site as the pocket where the substrate fits in the model.
examples.zh: 图中用凹槽标出模型中的「酶活性位点」，底物可在这里结合。

examples.en: We identified the enzyme active site before mapping it to the corresponding reaction on the chart.
examples.zh: 我们先辨认「酶活性位点」，再把它与图表上相应的反应对应起来。

collocations: substrate binding at an enzyme active site
a pocket at an enzyme active site

words.enDefinition: The temporary complex formed when a substrate binds to an enzyme.

examples.en: The middle panel shows the enzyme-substrate complex before the model displays any released product.
examples.zh: 中间一幅图展示了模型中尚未释放产物时的「酶–底物复合物」。

examples.en: We labeled the enzyme-substrate complex where the two shapes were shown together at the binding site.
examples.zh: 我们在结合位点处两个形状靠在一起的位置标出了「酶–底物复合物」。

collocations: a diagram of an enzyme-substrate complex

words.enDefinition: The capacity of an enzyme to speed a particular reaction under stated conditions.

examples.en: The lesson interpreted catalytic activity using two simulated traces for the same human enzyme reaction.
examples.zh: 课程用同一人体酶反应的两条模拟曲线来解读「催化活性」。

examples.en: We read the chart's description of catalytic activity before comparing the slopes shown on its graph.
examples.zh: 比较图中斜率之前，我们先读了图表关于「催化活性」的说明。

collocations: the catalytic activity of an enzyme

words.enDefinition: The energy barrier that a reaction must overcome to proceed along a given pathway.

examples.en: The diagram draws activation energy as the height of a barrier above the starting level.
examples.zh: 图中用起始水平上方能垒的高度表示「活化能」。

examples.en: We compared activation energy on two schematic paths that led to the same final product.
examples.zh: 我们比较通向同一最终产物的两条示意路径上各自的「活化能」。

collocations: the activation energy of a reaction

words.enDefinition: Preferential stabilization of a reaction's transition state relative to its starting state, lowering the barrier.

examples.en: The textbook illustrates transition state stabilization with a lower peak on the catalyzed reaction diagram.
examples.zh: 教材用催化反应图上较低的峰表示「过渡态稳定化」。

examples.en: We discussed transition state stabilization after comparing the peak heights in the two energy diagrams.
examples.zh: 我们比较两幅能量图的峰高后，讨论了「过渡态稳定化」。

collocations: a model of transition state stabilization
transition state stabilization by an enzyme

words.enDefinition: The extent to which an enzyme recognizes particular substrates rather than acting equally on others.

examples.en: The diagram demonstrates substrate specificity by showing one illustrated molecule recognized and another left unbound.
examples.zh: 图中一个分子被识别，另一个未结合，以此展示「底物特异性」。

examples.en: We used the labeled shapes to explain substrate specificity in the simplified model of a human enzyme.
examples.zh: 我们用标明的形状解释简化人体酶模型中的「底物特异性」。

words.enDefinition: A binding model in which an enzyme changes its shape as the substrate binds.

examples.en: The animation illustrates induced fit as the enzyme pocket shifts slightly after the substrate begins binding.
examples.zh: 动画中，底物开始结合后酶的凹槽略有改变，以此展示「诱导契合」。

examples.en: We compared the two frames to identify the shape change associated with induced fit in the diagram.
examples.zh: 我们比较两帧画面，以辨认图中「诱导契合」所伴随的形状变化。

collocations: induced fit at an enzyme's active site

words.enDefinition: A regulatory binding site separate from an enzyme's active site.

examples.en: The diagram marks an allosteric site away from the enzyme pocket that binds the substrate.
examples.zh: 图中在与底物结合的酶凹槽之外，标出一个「变构位点」。

examples.en: We used different colors for the allosteric site and the active site in our classroom sketch.
examples.zh: 课堂草图里，我们用不同颜色表示「变构位点」和活性位点。

collocations: a molecule bound at an allosteric site
the location of an allosteric site

words.enDefinition: Control of enzyme activity through binding at a site distinct from the active site.

examples.en: The classroom figure illustrates allosteric regulation by showing a change at one site after binding elsewhere.
examples.zh: 课堂图展示某处结合后另一处发生变化，以此说明「变构调节」。

examples.en: We traced the arrow linking the regulatory site to a change in activity during allosteric regulation.
examples.zh: 我们顺着箭头观察「变构调节」如何将调节位点与活性变化联系起来。

collocations: allosteric regulation of a metabolic enzyme

words.enDefinition: Regulation in which a product of a metabolic pathway reduces activity at an earlier step.

examples.en: In the classroom map, feedback inhibition sends a regulatory arrow from the final product toward an earlier enzyme.
examples.zh: 课堂图用从最终产物指向上游酶的调节箭头，表示「反馈抑制」。

examples.en: We located feedback inhibition by finding where the end product reduced activity earlier in the pathway.
examples.zh: 我们找到终产物降低途径上游活性的位置，据此定位「反馈抑制」。

words.enDefinition: A nonprotein component, such as a metal ion or organic molecule, required for an enzyme's activity.

examples.en: The diagram shows an enzyme cofactor as a separate component next to the folded protein chain.
examples.zh: 图中在折叠蛋白质链旁画出一个独立组分，表示「酶辅因子」。

examples.en: We labeled the enzyme cofactor before comparing the complete structure with the protein alone in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先标出「酶辅因子」，再把完整结构与单独的蛋白质作比较。

collocations: the function of an enzyme cofactor

words.enDefinition: An organic cofactor involved in an enzyme-catalyzed reaction, often carrying a group or electrons.

examples.en: The pathway drawing shows a coenzyme carrying electrons from one step of human metabolism to another.
examples.zh: 代谢图显示，「辅酶」将电子从人体代谢的一个步骤带到另一个步骤。

examples.en: We identified the coenzyme symbol before following its change between the two reaction arrows in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先辨认「辅酶」符号，再观察它在两个反应箭头之间的变化。

words.enDefinition: A nonprotein cofactor that remains tightly bound to its associated protein.

examples.en: The textbook marks the prosthetic group as a small component held firmly inside the folded protein.
examples.zh: 教材把「辅基」标为牢固结合在折叠蛋白质内部的小组分。

examples.en: We compared the prosthetic group with a separate cofactor drawn moving between steps in the diagram.
examples.zh: 我们把「辅基」与图中画成在不同步骤之间移动的独立辅因子作比较。

collocations: the function of a prosthetic group

words.enDefinition: The protein part of an enzyme without its required cofactor.

examples.en: The first panel labels the apoenzyme before the required nonprotein component appears in the next frame.
examples.zh: 第一幅图标出「脱辅基酶」，所需的非蛋白组分在下一帧才出现。

examples.en: We compared the apoenzyme with the complete enzyme shown beside it in the classroom drawing.
examples.zh: 我们把「脱辅基酶」与课堂图中旁边的完整酶进行了比较。

words.enDefinition: An enzyme in its complete form with the cofactors required for catalytic activity.

examples.en: The holoenzyme in the illustration includes the protein and its required cofactor in one assembled form.
examples.zh: 图中的「全酶」由蛋白质及其所需辅因子共同组成。

examples.en: We found the holoenzyme in the final panel where the textbook shows both components together.
examples.zh: 我们在教材最后一幅同时画出两个组分的图里找到了「全酶」。

words.enDefinition: The study of how fast enzyme-catalyzed reactions occur and what affects their rates.

examples.en: The enzyme kinetics chapter uses a simulated graph to relate substrate concentration to reaction rate.
examples.zh: 「酶动力学」一章用模拟图说明底物浓度与反应速率的关系。

examples.en: We used enzyme kinetics to interpret why the two labeled curves rose at different rates in the model.
examples.zh: 我们用「酶动力学」解释模型中两条标记曲线为何以不同速率上升。

words.enDefinition: The reaction rate measured or modeled near the start, before concentrations change substantially.

examples.en: We read the initial reaction rate from the slope at the beginning of the simulated product curve.
examples.zh: 我们从模拟产物曲线起始部分的斜率读出「初始反应速率」。

examples.en: The table listed an initial reaction rate for each example in the human enzyme model.
examples.zh: 表格列出人体酶模型中各个示例的「初始反应速率」。

collocations: an initial reaction rate on a plot
the initial reaction rate of an enzyme

words.enDefinition: The amount of substrate per unit volume in a reaction system.

examples.en: The horizontal axis shows substrate concentration in our simulated graph of the human enzyme reaction.
examples.zh: 模拟人体酶反应图的横轴表示「底物浓度」。

examples.en: We found the substrate concentration corresponding to a labeled point on the curve in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂模型上找出曲线某个标记点所对应的「底物浓度」。

collocations: reaction rate at a particular substrate concentration

words.enDefinition: A high-substrate condition in a simple enzyme model where substrate occupies nearly all active sites and the reaction rate approaches its limiting rate.

examples.en: In the model, enzyme saturation appeared as a plateau where the rate increased very little.
examples.zh: 模型中的「酶饱和」表现为一个平台，此处反应速率增加很少。

examples.en: We linked enzyme saturation to the sketch showing most active sites occupied at the same time.
examples.zh: 我们将「酶饱和」联系到草图中同一时刻大多数活性位点都已被占据的画面。

words.enDefinition: The limiting reaction rate of a fixed amount of enzyme as substrate becomes saturating in the model.

examples.en: The dashed line represents maximum reaction velocity where the simulated curve approaches its upper plateau.
examples.zh: 虚线表示模拟曲线接近上方平台时对应的「最大反应速率」。

examples.en: We found half the maximum reaction velocity on the hypothetical curve used in class.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂使用的假设曲线上找出了「最大反应速率」的一半。

collocations: maximum reaction velocity in an enzyme model

words.enDefinition: In the Michaelis-Menten model, the substrate concentration at which the reaction rate is half its maximum.

examples.en: The Michaelis constant was marked below the point where the model reached half its maximum rate.
examples.zh: 模型达到最大速率一半的那个点下方标出了「米氏常数」。

examples.en: We used the labeled concentration axis to locate the Michaelis constant in the simulated diagram.
examples.zh: 我们根据标注的浓度轴，在模拟图中找出「米氏常数」。

collocations: the Michaelis constant of a modeled enzyme

words.enDefinition: Reversible inhibition in which a substrate and inhibitor cannot bind to the same enzyme simultaneously.

examples.en: The diagram illustrates competitive inhibition with two shapes competing for the same pocket on the model enzyme.
examples.zh: 示意图用两个形状竞争模型酶上的同一个凹槽，来展示「竞争性抑制」。

examples.en: We identified competitive inhibition in the conceptual drawing because the two shapes could bind only in turn.
examples.zh: 概念图中，两个形状不能同时结合，我们据此辨认出「竞争性抑制」。

words.enDefinition: Reversible inhibition in which the inhibitor binds only to the enzyme-substrate complex.

examples.en: The uncompetitive inhibition panel shows the second shape binding only after the substrate is already present.
examples.zh: 「反竞争性抑制」图中，底物已经结合后，第二个形状才发生结合。

examples.en: We identified uncompetitive inhibition by noting which enzyme state was shown with the bound regulatory molecule.
examples.zh: 我们观察调节分子结合时酶处于何种状态，据此辨认出「反竞争性抑制」。

words.enDefinition: In the pure noncompetitive model, reversible inhibition in which the inhibitor binds free enzyme and enzyme already bound to substrate with equal affinity.

examples.en: The diagram shows noncompetitive inhibition with the regulatory shape binding whether the substrate is present or absent.
examples.zh: 图中无论底物是否已结合，调节分子形状都可与酶结合，用以展示「非竞争性抑制」。

examples.en: Our class read the noncompetitive inhibition panel as an ideal model with equal binding in both states.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们把「非竞争性抑制」图解读为两种状态下结合能力相同的理想模型。

words.enDefinition: An increase in enzyme activity caused by binding at a regulatory site distinct from the active site.

examples.en: The regulatory arrow in the textbook links allosteric activation to higher activity in the human enzyme model.
examples.zh: 教材中的调节箭头将「变构激活」与人体酶模型中更高的活性联系起来。

examples.en: We found allosteric activation where a regulatory shape bound away from the enzyme's active site.
examples.zh: 我们在调节分子形状结合于酶活性位点以外的位置，找到了「变构激活」的标示。

collocations: allosteric activation of a metabolic enzyme

words.enDefinition: A nucleotide with three phosphate groups that couples energy-releasing and energy-requiring processes in cells.

examples.en: The textbook labels adenosine triphosphate beside the arrow linking an energy source to a cellular task.
examples.zh: 教材在连接能量来源与一项细胞活动的箭头旁标出「三磷酸腺苷」。

examples.en: We counted three phosphate groups on adenosine triphosphate in the enlarged molecular diagram used in class.
examples.zh: 我们数出课堂放大分子图上的「三磷酸腺苷」有三个磷酸基团。

collocations: the phosphate groups of adenosine triphosphate

words.enDefinition: A nucleotide with two phosphate groups that can be converted to ATP in cells.

examples.en: The diagram shows adenosine diphosphate beside a separate phosphate group after the reaction in the model.
examples.zh: 在模型反应完成后，图中把「二磷酸腺苷」画在一个独立的磷酸基团旁边。

examples.en: We identified adenosine diphosphate by counting two phosphate groups in the classroom drawing of the molecule.
examples.zh: 我们数出课堂分子图中有两个磷酸基团，据此认出「二磷酸腺苷」。

collocations: adenosine diphosphate in a reaction diagram
the phosphate groups of adenosine diphosphate

words.enDefinition: The cleavage of ATP by water, often yielding ADP and inorganic phosphate.

examples.en: The model shows ATP hydrolysis producing ADP and inorganic phosphate during normal activity in a human cell.
examples.zh: 模型显示，人体细胞正常活动时，「ATP 水解」生成 ADP 和无机磷酸盐。

examples.en: We located ATP hydrolysis on the energy diagram before following the next coupled reaction in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们先在能量图中找出「ATP 水解」，再看紧随其后的偶联反应。

words.enDefinition: The continual consumption and regeneration of ATP in cells, often described as a rate.

examples.en: The lecture linked ATP turnover to the continual use and replacement of ATP in an active muscle cell.
examples.zh: 课程把「ATP 周转」与活动肌细胞中 ATP 持续消耗和再生联系起来。

examples.en: The two arrows represent ATP turnover even when the amount present stays similar in the model.
examples.zh: 即使模型中的 ATP 含量保持大致不变，两个箭头仍表示「ATP 周转」。

words.enDefinition: Linking a favorable process to an unfavorable one so their net free energy change favors both proceeding together.

examples.en: The schematic explains energy coupling by showing ATP hydrolysis driving a reaction that requires energy.
examples.zh: 示意图展示 ATP 水解如何推动一个需要能量的反应，以解释「能量偶联」。

examples.en: We marked the arrow that showed energy coupling between the two processes in the human cell model.
examples.zh: 我们在人体细胞模型里标出两种过程发生「能量偶联」的箭头。

words.enDefinition: A series of linked cellular reactions in which products of earlier steps can serve as later reactants.

examples.en: We followed the metabolic pathway from its initial compound to the final product on the classroom chart.
examples.zh: 我们从起始化合物沿课堂图表上的「代谢途径」追踪到最终产物。

examples.en: The metabolic pathway on the worksheet branched at a compound shared by two sets of reactions.
examples.zh: 习题中的「代谢途径」在两组反应共享的一种化合物处出现分支。

collocations: a branch in a metabolic pathway

words.enDefinition: A substance formed at one metabolic step and used at a subsequent step.

examples.en: The diagram labels pyruvate as an intermediate metabolite linking glucose breakdown with another set of reactions.
examples.zh: 图中把丙酮酸标为连接葡萄糖分解与另一组反应的「代谢中间产物」。

examples.en: We identified the intermediate metabolite produced by the first arrow and consumed at the next step.
examples.zh: 我们找出第一个箭头所示反应生成、又在下一步被消耗的「代谢中间产物」。

collocations: an intermediate metabolite on a pathway
an intermediate metabolite shared by pathways

words.enDefinition: Cellular metabolism that breaks down substances, often providing energy for other activities.

examples.en: The textbook uses glucose breakdown to illustrate catabolism in the chapter on how human cells obtain energy.
examples.zh: 教材在人体细胞如何获取能量一章用葡萄糖分解说明「分解代谢」。

examples.en: We identified catabolism where the pathway diagram showed a large storage molecule yielding smaller units.
examples.zh: 我们在代谢图上大储存分子分解为较小单元的位置，辨认「分解代谢」。

words.enDefinition: Cellular metabolism that builds larger or more complex molecules and typically requires an energy input.

examples.en: The map lists glycogen formation under anabolism because the cell builds a larger storage molecule.
examples.zh: 代谢图把糖原形成归为「合成代谢」，因为细胞形成了较大的储存分子。

examples.en: We used the direction of the arrows to identify anabolism on the classroom diagram of metabolism.
examples.zh: 我们根据箭头方向，在课堂代谢图中辨认「合成代谢」。

words.enDefinition: In humans, the collection of processes extracting energy from nutrients and ultimately transferring electrons to oxygen.

examples.en: The cellular respiration chart connects energy from nutrients to ATP production in an ordinary human cell.
examples.zh: 「细胞呼吸」图将营养物质提供的能量与普通人体细胞生成 ATP 联系起来。

examples.en: We used the cellular respiration diagram to distinguish the cytoplasmic stage from reactions inside the mitochondrion.
examples.zh: 我们用「细胞呼吸」图辨别细胞质中的阶段与线粒体内部的反应。

words.enDefinition: ATP production by glycolysis without requiring oxygen, with pyruvate reduced to lactate to regenerate NAD+.

examples.en: The muscle cell diagram shows anaerobic glycolysis supplying ATP while the pathway converts pyruvate to lactate.
examples.zh: 肌细胞图显示，「无氧糖酵解」供应 ATP，此时途径将丙酮酸转化为乳酸根。

examples.en: We identified anaerobic glycolysis from the branch ending in lactate on the classroom energy map.
examples.zh: 我们根据课堂能量图中终点为乳酸根的分支，辨认「无氧糖酵解」。

words.enDefinition: A cytoplasmic pathway converting glucose to pyruvate while producing ATP and reduced electron carriers.

examples.en: The diagram places glycolysis in the cytoplasm and labels pyruvate as the product of the pathway.
examples.zh: 图中将「糖酵解」标在细胞质内，并把丙酮酸标为该途径的产物。

examples.en: We traced glycolysis across the worksheet to see where ATP was used and later produced.
examples.zh: 我们沿习题追踪「糖酵解」，查看 ATP 在哪里被消耗，又在哪里生成。

words.enDefinition: The three-carbon end product of glycolysis, present mainly as the ion of pyruvic acid in cells.

examples.en: The simplified pathway shows pyruvate at the end of glycolysis and before its different possible fates.
examples.zh: 简化代谢图将「丙酮酸」放在糖酵解的终点、不同后续去向之前。

examples.en: We circled pyruvate at the branch connecting the sugar pathway to the mitochondrion in the diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在图中连接糖代谢途径与线粒体的分支处圈出了「丙酮酸」。

words.enDefinition: The ion of lactic acid, formed from pyruvate in human cells and usable in other metabolic pathways.

examples.en: The chart shows lactate as a product formed from pyruvate in the illustrated muscle cell.
examples.zh: 图中把「乳酸」标为所示肌细胞由丙酮酸形成的产物。

examples.en: We followed an arrow showing lactate entering another pathway in the overview of human metabolism.
examples.zh: 我们顺着人体代谢总览图中的箭头，观察「乳酸」进入另一条途径。

words.enDefinition: The conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA, releasing carbon dioxide and producing NADH in human mitochondria.

examples.en: The metabolism map places pyruvate oxidation between glycolysis and the citric acid cycle in human cells.
examples.zh: 人体细胞代谢图把「丙酮酸氧化」标在糖酵解与柠檬酸循环之间。

examples.en: We located the carbon dioxide symbol on the arrow labeled pyruvate oxidation in the classroom diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂图中标着「丙酮酸氧化」的箭头上找到了二氧化碳符号。

words.enDefinition: Coenzyme A carrying an acetyl group that can enter central metabolic pathways.

examples.en: The diagram shows acetyl-CoA carrying a two-carbon group into the citric acid cycle in a human cell.
examples.zh: 图中显示，「乙酰辅酶 A」将一个二碳基团带入人体细胞的柠檬酸循环。

examples.en: We found acetyl-CoA where arrows from two different sources met on the classroom map of metabolism.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂代谢图上两个不同来源的箭头交汇处找到了「乙酰辅酶 A」。

collocations: acetyl-CoA entering the citric acid cycle
transfer of an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA

words.enDefinition: A mitochondrial cycle that oxidizes acetyl groups, releases carbon dioxide, and transfers electrons to carriers.

examples.en: The circular diagram of the citric acid cycle shows how several intermediates are converted and regenerated.
examples.zh: 「柠檬酸循环」的环形图展示了若干中间产物如何转化和再生。

examples.en: We traced the citric acid cycle while noting which steps transferred electrons to the depicted carriers.
examples.zh: 我们沿「柠檬酸循环」观察，同时记下哪些步骤将电子转移给图示载体。

collocations: an intermediate of the citric acid cycle
reactions of the citric acid cycle

words.enDefinition: The ion of citric acid, formed at the entry to the citric acid cycle.

examples.en: The figure places citrate after the step that combines an acetyl group with a four-carbon compound.
examples.zh: 图中把「柠檬酸」标在乙酰基与一个四碳化合物结合的步骤之后。

examples.en: We circled citrate on the pathway map beside the drawing of its six carbon atoms.
examples.zh: 我们在代谢图上六个碳原子的示意结构旁圈出了「柠檬酸」。

collocations: citrate in the citric acid cycle

words.enDefinition: A four-carbon intermediate that accepts an acetyl group in the first step of the citric acid cycle.

examples.en: The diagram shows oxaloacetate regenerated at the end of one turn of the citric acid cycle.
examples.zh: 图中显示，「草酰乙酸」在柠檬酸循环每完成一轮时再生。

examples.en: We colored oxaloacetate before tracing its four carbons through the first drawn step of the cycle.
examples.zh: 我们先给「草酰乙酸」着色，再沿循环图第一步追踪它的四个碳原子。

collocations: oxaloacetate in the citric acid cycle

words.enDefinition: The reduced form of NAD that carries electrons between metabolic reactions.

examples.en: The chart shows NADH carrying electrons toward the inner mitochondrial membrane in the human cell model.
examples.zh: 图中显示，在人体细胞模型中，「还原型 NAD」把电子带向线粒体内膜。

examples.en: We marked NADH beside the reactions that transferred electrons onto the carrier in the pathway diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在代谢图上把「还原型 NAD」标在将电子转移给这种载体的反应旁。

words.enDefinition: The electron-accepting form of the coenzyme NAD, also written NAD plus.

examples.en: The textbook labels oxidized NAD where the carrier accepts electrons during glucose breakdown in the cytoplasm.
examples.zh: 教材在细胞质内葡萄糖分解中该载体接受电子的位置标出了「氧化型 NAD」。

examples.en: We found oxidized NAD on the diagram after the electron carrier released its electrons at another step.
examples.zh: 当电子载体在另一个步骤释放电子后，我们在图上找出了「氧化型 NAD」。

words.enDefinition: The reduced form of flavin adenine dinucleotide that carries electrons during metabolism.

examples.en: The diagram marks FADH2 beside the step in which an enzyme's bound carrier accepts electrons.
examples.zh: 图中在酶结合的载体接受电子的一步旁标出了「还原型 FAD」。

examples.en: We followed the electrons associated with FADH2 on the map of normal mitochondrial energy metabolism.
examples.zh: 我们在正常线粒体能量代谢图上追踪「还原型 FAD」所携带的电子。

words.enDefinition: A series of mitochondrial proteins transferring electrons to oxygen and using the released energy to build a gradient.

examples.en: The electron transport chain appears along the inner mitochondrial membrane on the simplified human cell diagram.
examples.zh: 简化的人体细胞图将「电子传递链」画在线粒体内膜上。

examples.en: We traced electrons through the electron transport chain to the oxygen symbol at the end.
examples.zh: 我们沿「电子传递链」追踪电子，直到末端的氧符号。

collocations: electron flow through the electron transport chain
a diagram of the electron transport chain

words.enDefinition: A difference in proton concentration between two sides of a membrane.

examples.en: The textbook depicts a proton gradient by drawing more protons on one side of the inner membrane.
examples.zh: 教材在线粒体内膜一侧画出较多的质子，以表示「质子梯度」。

examples.en: We marked the proton gradient on the mitochondrial model beside the labels for its two compartments.
examples.zh: 我们在线粒体模型两个区室的标记旁标出了「质子梯度」。

collocations: a proton gradient across a membrane
a diagram of a proton gradient

words.enDefinition: ATP synthesis powered by the proton electrochemical gradient maintained by mitochondrial electron transport.

examples.en: The classroom map connects oxidative phosphorylation with the electron carriers that release electrons at the inner membrane.
examples.zh: 课堂图把「氧化磷酸化」与在线粒体内膜释放电子的电子载体联系起来。

examples.en: We placed oxidative phosphorylation next to the model showing ATP formation driven by proton movement.
examples.zh: 我们在表示质子移动驱动 ATP 形成的模型旁标出「氧化磷酸化」。

words.enDefinition: The enzyme that makes ATP using energy from protons moving across a membrane.

examples.en: The mitochondrial drawing labels ATP synthase where protons return across the inner membrane toward the matrix.
examples.zh: 线粒体图在质子跨内膜回到基质的位置标出了「ATP 合酶」。

examples.en: We identified ATP synthase next to the arrow showing the formation of ATP in the model.
examples.zh: 我们在模型中表示 ATP 形成的箭头旁找到了「ATP 合酶」。

words.enDefinition: Direct formation of ATP or an equivalent nucleotide by transferring a phosphate from a metabolic intermediate.

examples.en: The pathway figure shows substrate-level phosphorylation at a step that directly transfers a phosphate group to ADP.
examples.zh: 代谢图把将磷酸基团直接转移到 ADP 的一步画成「底物水平磷酸化」。

examples.en: We marked substrate-level phosphorylation on the glycolysis diagram beside the arrow showing ATP formation in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们在糖酵解图中表示 ATP 形成的箭头旁标注了「底物水平磷酸化」。

words.enDefinition: Repeated breakdown of fatty acyl chains that releases two-carbon acetyl units and transfers electrons to carriers.

examples.en: The map shows fatty acid beta-oxidation shortening a long chain as acetyl units appear in the diagram.
examples.zh: 代谢图显示，「脂肪酸 β 氧化」使长链缩短，同时出现乙酰基单元。

examples.en: We located fatty acid beta-oxidation on the pathway chart connecting stored fat to central energy metabolism.
examples.zh: 我们在连接储存脂肪与中央能量代谢的图上找到了「脂肪酸 β 氧化」。

collocations: a map of fatty acid beta-oxidation

words.enDefinition: Formation of glucose from noncarbohydrate precursors such as lactate, glycerol, or certain amino acids.

examples.en: The diagram shows gluconeogenesis linking a noncarbohydrate starting molecule to glucose production in normal human metabolism.
examples.zh: 图中「糖异生」将非糖类起始分子与正常人体代谢中的葡萄糖生成联系起来。

examples.en: We traced glycerol toward the glucose label on the classroom chart that illustrates gluconeogenesis in humans.
examples.zh: 我们在展示人体「糖异生」的课堂图表上，从甘油一路追踪到葡萄糖标记。

words.enDefinition: The cellular formation of glycogen from glucose-derived building blocks.

examples.en: The diagram represents glycogenesis with arrows adding glucose units to a branched storage molecule in muscle.
examples.zh: 图中用将葡萄糖单元加到肌肉中支链储存分子的箭头表示「糖原合成」。

examples.en: We identified glycogenesis on the muscle cell map where the glucose reserve became larger in the model.
examples.zh: 我们在肌细胞图中葡萄糖储备增加的位置辨认出了「糖原合成」。

words.enDefinition: Breakdown of glycogen, releasing most of its glucose units as glucose-1-phosphate.

examples.en: The classroom drawing shows glycogenolysis supplying glucose phosphate from a branched storage molecule in muscle.
examples.zh: 课堂图画出肌肉中的支链储存分子经「糖原分解」释放葡萄糖磷酸衍生物。

examples.en: We followed glycogenolysis in the map while locating the unit released from the stored chain.
examples.zh: 我们在代谢图中沿「糖原分解」观察，同时找出从储存链上释放的单元。

words.enDefinition: A glucose-linked pathway producing NADPH and sugar phosphates, including five-carbon intermediates.

examples.en: The pentose phosphate pathway appears as a branch from glucose metabolism on our classroom human cell diagram.
examples.zh: 课堂人体细胞图把「磷酸戊糖途径」画成葡萄糖代谢的一条分支。

examples.en: We located NADPH among the products shown beside the pentose phosphate pathway in the textbook chart.
examples.zh: 我们在教材图上「磷酸戊糖途径」旁所列的产物中找到了 NADPH。

collocations: the oxidative part of the pentose phosphate pathway
NADPH from the pentose phosphate pathway
a diagram of the pentose phosphate pathway

words.enDefinition: The reduced form of NADP, used to supply electrons for cellular synthesis and other reactions.

examples.en: The map shows NADPH donating electrons during a reaction that builds a larger cellular molecule.
examples.zh: 代谢图显示，「还原型 NADP」在形成一个较大细胞分子的反应中提供电子。

examples.en: We marked NADPH next to the branch that supplies reducing power in the classroom metabolism diagram.
examples.zh: 我们在课堂代谢图中提供还原能力的分支旁标出了「还原型 NADP」。

collocations: use of NADPH in cellular synthesis

words.enDefinition: A water-soluble energy metabolite made mainly in the liver from fatty acid-derived acetyl-CoA.

examples.en: The human metabolism chart shows a ketone body as an alternative fuel for some body tissues.
examples.zh: 人体代谢图把一种「酮体」列为部分人体组织的另一种能量来源。

examples.en: We identified the ketone body where the diagram linked fat breakdown with another route for energy use.
examples.zh: 我们在图中把脂肪分解与另一条供能途径联系起来的位置找到了「酮体」。

collocations: a ketone body used for energy
a ketone body on a pathway diagram

words.enDefinition: Cellular formation of fatty acids from smaller carbon-containing precursors, often followed by fat storage.

examples.en: The metabolism diagram links lipogenesis to the formation of fatty acids from smaller molecules in cells.
examples.zh: 代谢图将「脂肪生成」与细胞用小分子形成脂肪酸联系起来。

examples.en: We located lipogenesis on the normal human cell map beside the arrow pointing toward lipid storage.
examples.zh: 我们在正常人体细胞图中指向脂质储存的箭头旁找到了「脂肪生成」。

words.enDefinition: The breakdown of stored triacylglycerol, releasing fatty acids and glycerol.

examples.en: The lipolysis panel shows fatty acids and glycerol leaving a triacylglycerol molecule in the classroom model.
examples.zh: 课堂「脂解」图显示，脂肪酸和甘油从甘油三酯分子释放出来。

examples.en: We traced lipolysis on the map before comparing the separate fates of glycerol and fatty acids.
examples.zh: 我们先在图中沿「脂解」途径追踪，再比较甘油与脂肪酸各自的去向。

words.enDefinition: Transfer of an amino group from one amino acid to a keto acid.

examples.en: The classroom chart illustrates transamination by showing an amino group move from one molecule to another.
examples.zh: 课堂图画出一个氨基从一个分子转至另一个分子，以说明「转氨作用」。

examples.en: We marked transamination where the worksheet linked an amino acid with its corresponding keto acid.
examples.zh: 我们在习题把氨基酸与相应酮酸联系起来的位置标明「转氨作用」。

collocations: an amino group transferred by transamination

words.enDefinition: Removal of an amino group from an amino acid, sometimes releasing ammonium.

examples.en: The diagram labels amino acid deamination at the step where a nitrogen group leaves the molecule.
examples.zh: 图中在含氮基团离开分子的一步标出了「氨基酸脱氨」。

examples.en: We compared amino acid deamination with the separate transfer reaction shown elsewhere on the classroom chart.
examples.zh: 我们把「氨基酸脱氨」与课堂图中另一处画出的转移反应作了比较。

collocations: an example of amino acid deamination
nitrogen released during amino acid deamination
a diagram of amino acid deamination

words.enDefinition: The rate at which material passes through a reaction or pathway in metabolism.

examples.en: The simulated diagram uses thicker arrows to represent higher metabolic flux through the glucose pathway.
examples.zh: 模拟图用较粗的箭头表示单位时间内有更多物质通过葡萄糖代谢途径，即更高的「代谢通量」。

examples.en: We compared metabolic flux at two branches on the classroom chart using the modeled rates.
examples.zh: 我们根据模型速率，比较课堂图上两条分支的「代谢通量」。
